justification: A typed 450 m2 decided which rules a user sees, for every council. Standard: one pure function, one new optional prop on three sections.

pre_impl.existing_data: constraints.minLotSize from the Planning Portal Lot Size layer (frontend-nextjs/lib/nsw-planning-portal.ts:782)
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: No Lot Size layer for the address gives null, so nothing is hidden
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Render-time only, every page view from deploy

functions.name: canSubdivide
functions.input: lot area as number or text, plus the LEP minimum lot size
functions.if_none: either value missing returns true so rows show

break_it.scenario: A 300 m2 lot in a council whose LEP minimum is 200 m2
break_it.what_happens: Before: subdivision rules hidden as too small. Now: shown

break_it.scenario: The address has no Lot Size layer so minLotSize is null
break_it.what_happens: All subdivision rules are shown, none hidden

break_it.scenario: A lot just above the minimum that still cannot make two lots
break_it.what_happens: Subdivision rules show; user reads them, nothing wrongly hidden
break_it.how: Showing is the safe side; hiding needs the LEP figure

falsifiable_check.observed_red: Ran the new test against the unfixed function: 3 failed, 2 passed.
